newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Shell considers withdrawal from PVC production.
newsitem.headline: Shell considers withdrawal from PVC production.

text.p: Parts of Royal Dutch/Shell's chemicals division may be shed if they continue to underperform, one of Shell's director said in an interview in this month's company magazine, Shell Venster.

The company's chemicals division has achieved a return on average capital employed of nine percent in the ten years from 1985 and, Evert Henkes, director of Stategy and Business Services for chemicals, said this was unacceptable.

"Our return of nine percent is much too low when compared with industry leaders which manage a return of 12 to 15 percent," Henkes said. The focus of Henkes attention is the company's PVC (polyvinyl chloride) and epoxy resin production units.
"Thinking of my shareholders, I have to recognise that the PVC industry is not going through a flourishing time. The question is, when can we come out of that rut," Henkes said.
Henkes spelled out that the operations must either improve their performance, possibly via joint ventures or mergers, or they will be sold off.
Shell spokesman Henk Bonder told Reuters on Wednesday that the sale of units was not a near-term objective. Units would only be sold if they prove incapable of improvement, he said.
"If this group of products is not able to perform in a world-class manner, then there could be the possibility that we pull out," Bonder said.
Bonder said the sectors under scrutiny represented 20-25 percent of Shell Chemicals worldwide.
Shell produces PVC at its Pernis site in Rotterdam and in Berre in France. Epoxy resin production is worldwide.
Shell's rationalisation of its chemicals divisions has already involved the divestment of Shell Fine Chemicals, sold to Inspec Group Plc in July.
